From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <ops@atlasretail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:03:10 -0000
Subject: Root cause and mitigation applied — 429s (update)

Hi all — quick update from infra: root cause identified and mitigated.

What happened (summary):
- At 08:30 UTC we deployed an automated quota policy change intended to tighten global token thresholds for a small set of non-production tenants.
- A broadened selector in the policy caused the enforcement to be evaluated at per-tenant scope rather than per-project scope for a subset of customers, including Atlas Retail. This made the policy apply more aggressively and triggered sudden 429s when normal traffic patterns hit the tightened counters.

Mitigation steps taken (completed at 10:45 UTC):
- Rolled back the policy push to the prior ruleset.
- Deployed an emergency bypass rule for affected tenants while we validate the rollback.
- Increased short-term enforcement thresholds for Atlas Retail to prevent recurrence during validation.
- Added temporary routing to a compatible model variant with slightly higher latency but much higher token headroom (no change to your SLA metrics collected on Redwood console).

Current status: 429s dropped back to baseline at ~10:50 UTC and we've seen normal traffic patterns through 11:00 UTC. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps (we own):
- Prepare a short postmortem with timeline and corrective actions (draft attached: postmortem-draft.md).
- Introduce stronger validation in policy rollout tooling to prevent selector broadening regressions.
- Add an automated canary that verifies quota calculations at tenant granularity for live traffic samples before global enforcement.

Emma — apologies for the impact. We'll share a formal follow-up with action items and ETA on the permanent fixes by EOD tomorrow. If you'd like a technical deep-dive call, we can schedule one — suggested times in my calendar are attached.

— Evelyn

Subject: Follow-up: Incident summary, credits, and long-term action items

Hi Emma / Procurement,

Following up with the formal summary and next steps after the 11/9 incident. Thank you for your patience — we know this impacted production traffic and appreciate the timely signal from your team.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:30 UTC — policy push that inadvertently broadened selector scope
- ~08:55 UTC — spike in 429s reported by Atlas (sample logs received)
- 09:12 UTC — Redwood on-call acknowledged and began triage
- 10:45 UTC — rollback and emergency bypass applied
- 10:50 UTC — errors returned to baseline; ongoing monitoring

Root cause: a policy rollout bug that changed evaluation granularity for token-based quota enforcement. The change was intended for a limited set of non-prod tenants but matched production tenant selectors due to a mis-scoped label expression.

Customer impact: transient 429 failures (~12% of requests in window), increased latency for some flows during retries. We understand this affected user experience during your peak.

Planned corrective actions (committed):
- Hardening: rollout validation for policy selector semantics and an additional unit/integration check to catch scope expansion.
- Canarying: a live canary for quota enforcement that measures token counters at tenant granularity against representative traffic.
- Controls: a safe-mode guard that temporarily relaxes enforcement when error rates exceed configurable thresholds for specific tenants.
- Process: require a two-person approval for policy pushes touching production selector logic.

Customer remediation and credits:
- Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 15% of November usage for Atlas Retail to account for the impact window. Procurement, please confirm the billing contact and preferred process (we can route via the HubSpot deal DL-8421).

Attachments provided for your records: root_cause_patch.diff (proposed fix), incident_timeline.csv (detailed timestamps), postmortem-draft.md (internal draft).

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute technical review to walk through the remediation and answer any questions. Suggested slots: Thu 12 Nov 14:00-15:00 UTC or Fri 13 Nov 09:00-10:00 UTC. Please let me know what works and we'll send a calendar invite.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we'll follow through on the fixes and keep you updated.

Best,
